Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 34, verses 34–42:

When He, glory be to Him, related the condition of the disbelievers of earlier times, He followed it with what provides consolation to His Messenger, and with a clarification that the disbelief of the earlier nations toward the messengers sent to them is a continuing condition in the early ages. So He said: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town﴾ from among the towns, ﴿except that its affluent ones said﴾ that is, its leaders, its wealthy, its tyrants, and the leaders of evil toward their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent﴾ that is, in what you have been sent with of monotheism and faith. The clause ﴿except that its affluent ones said﴾ occupies a position of accusative (naṣb) as a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl).

Then He mentioned what they boasted of, namely wealth and children, and they measured their condition in the Hereafter by their condition in this world, on the supposition that what the messengers warned them of was true. So He said: ﴿And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ (p. 1200) The meaning is: God has favored us over you with wealth and children in this world, and this indicates that He is pleased with what we are upon of religion, and that we will not be punished in the Hereafter after His bounty to us in this world and His pleasure with us. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to answer on their behalf, and He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills"﴾ to extend it to him, ﴿and restricts [it]﴾ that is, He constricts it upon whom He wills to constrict it. He, glory be to Him, may provide for the disbeliever and the disobedient as a gradual leading on (istidrāj), and may test the obedient believer with restriction, multiplying his reward. Merely extending provision to one to whom He extends it does not indicate that He is pleased with him or with his deeds, nor does withholding it from one from whom He withholds it indicate that He is not pleased with him or with his deeds. So analogizing the Hereafter to this world in such a matter is a manifest error or an obvious sophistry. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ this. And among the majority of these are those who analogized the matter of the Hereafter to the former world. Then He reinforced this answer with affirmation and emphasis.

﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position﴾ that is, they are not the quality that brings you near to Us in nearness.

Mujahid said: "Zulfā" means nearness, and "zulfah" means closeness.

Al-Akhfash said: "Zulfā" is a verbal noun (ism al-maṣdar), as if he had said, "with that which brings you near to Us in bringing near," so "zulfā" is in the accusative position.

Al-Farra' said: "alladhī" here applies to both wealth and children together.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Your wealth is not what brings you near to Us in position, and your children are not a thing that brings you near to Us in position," and then the predicate of the first was deleted because the second indicates it. He recited:

"We are with what is ours, and you are with what is yours, content, though opinions differ."

It is permissible outside the Qur'an to say "bi-llatayn," "bi-llātī," "bi-llawātī," and "bi-lladhī" for children specifically. That is, wealth does not increase you in rank or elevation with Us, nor bring you near in any nearness ﴿except for one who believes and does righteous deeds﴾. This is a disjunctive exception (istithnā' munqaṭi'), so its position is accusative, meaning: "But whoever believes and does righteous deeds." Or it is in a genitive position as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "yuqarribukum" (bring you near). So said al-Zajjaj.

Al-Nahhas said: "This view is an error, because the particles kāf and mīm are for the addressee, and so substitution is not permissible. If this were permitted, one could say, 'I saw you Zayd.'"

It is answered that al-Akhfash and the Kufans permit that, and he said a view similar to the view of al-Zajjaj and al-Farra'. Al-Farra' also permitted that it be in a nominative position, meaning "it is only the one who believes." The reference in His words "fa-ulā'ika" (those) is to "man" (whoever), and the plural is according to its meaning. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿for them is the reward of double﴾, that is, the reward of an increase, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (Al-An'am 6:160). It is an attribution of the verbal noun to its object, that is, "the reward of multiplying the good deeds." It was said: "for them is the reward of multiplication," because "ḍi'f" has the sense of plurality. The "bā'" in "bi-mā 'amilū" (for what they did) indicates causation.

﴿And they will be in the lofty chambers, secure﴾ from everything they dislike. The intended meaning is the chambers of Paradise. The majority read "jazā' al-ḍi'f" with the genitive construction. Al-Zuhri, Ya'qub, Nasr ibn 'Asim, and Qatada read both words in the nominative case, with "al-ḍi'f" as a substitute (badal) for "jazā'."

It is narrated from Ya'qub that he read "jazā'an" in the accusative with tanwīn, and "al-ḍi'f" in the nominative, with the understanding: "So those will have the double as a reward," that is, as a state of its being a reward.

The majority read "fī al-ghurufāt" in the plural, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading because of His words: ﴿We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 29:58). Then He, glory be to Him, repeated what preceded for the purpose of emphasizing the proof and repelling what the disbelievers had said, so He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him"﴾, that is, He widens it for whom He wills and constricts it upon whom He wills. There is no indication in that of happiness or wretchedness. ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾, that is, He will replace it for you. It is said: "akhlafa lahu" and "akhlafa 'alayhi" when one gives him a substitute and replacement. That replacement is either in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾. The provision of servants to one another is only by God's facilitation and decree. They are not providers in reality, but only in a figurative sense, as one says of a man, "he provides for his dependents," and of a commander, "he provides for his soldiers." The true Provider of the commander and the commanded, the great and the small, is the One who created them. Whoever gives from among the servants to others some of what God has provided him, has only disposed of God's provision given to him. So by what he gives out, he deserves the reward for it, multiplied, for obeying God's command and spending as God commanded.

﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them all﴾. The adverbial phrase (ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed by a verb understood, such as "remember." Or it is connected to His words: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾ (Saba' 34:31). That is, if you could see them also on the Day He gathers them all for reckoning: the worshipper and the worshipped, the arrogant and the oppressed. Then We will say to the angels: ﴿Did these people used to worship you?﴾ as a reproach to the polytheists and a rebuke to whoever worships other than God, mighty and majestic, as in His words to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"﴾ (Al-Ma'idah 5:116). He singled out the angels for mention, although some disbelievers worshipped others besides them, such as devils and idols, because they are the most honored of what the polytheists worship.

Al-Nahhas said: The meaning is that if the angels deny them, that is a rebuke to the polytheists.

The clause ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our guardian, not them"﴾ is a resumptive sentence, answering an implied question, meaning: "Glory be to You; You are the One whom we take as protector, obey, and worship, not them. We did not take them as worshippers, nor did we take them as allies. We have no protector other than You." Then they explicitly stated what the polytheists used to worship, and said: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾, that is, the devils, who are Iblis and his soldiers. They claimed that they saw them, that they were angels, and that they were daughters of God. It was also said that they would enter the bellies of idols and speak to them from within. ﴿Most of them were believers in them﴾, that is, most of the polytheists believed in the jinn and accepted them as true. It was said: "The majority" here means "all."

﴿So today, none of you will possess for another benefit or harm﴾ (p. 1201). This refers to the worshippers and the worshipped: none of them, who are the worshipped, possesses for the others, who are the worshippers, any benefit, that is, intercession and salvation, nor any harm, that is, punishment and destruction. This statement is said to them to demonstrate their helplessness and inadequacy, and as a rebuke to those who worshipped them. His words "nor harm" are in the sense of an elided modifier, meaning: they do not possess for them the averting of harm. His words ﴿And We will say to those who wronged﴾ are coordinated with His words "He will say to the angels," meaning: to those who wronged themselves by worshipping other than God: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ in the world.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from Abu Razin, who said: There were two partners, one of whom went out to the coast while the other remained. When God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, he wrote to his companion asking him what had happened. He wrote back to him that no one from Quraysh had followed him except the rabble and the poor among the people. So he abandoned his trade and then went to his companion and said, "Show me to him." He was one who read the scriptures. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and said, "To what do you invite?" He said, "To such and such." He said, "I testify that you are the Messenger of God." He said, "What is your knowledge of that?" He said, "No prophet has ever been sent except that the rabble and the poor among the people followed him." Then these verses were revealed: ﴿We did not send a warner into any town except that its affluent ones said...﴾ and the rest of the verses. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, sent to him: "God has indeed revealed confirmation of what you said."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words "the reward of double," that he said: "It is the multiplication of the good deed."

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: When a man is wealthy and pious, God gives him his reward twice. He recited this verse: ﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children...﴾ until His words ﴿for them is the reward of double﴾, and said: "It is the multiplication of the good deed."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾ that he said: "Without extravagance and without stinginess." Similarly from Mujahid, and similarly from al-Hasan.

al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Jabir, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: "Whenever a servant spends an expenditure, God guarantees its replacement, except an expenditure in wrongdoing or disobedience."

Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil and al-Bayhaqi, through another chain from him, narrated something similar, traced back to the Prophet, and longer than it.

It is established in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "God, mighty and majestic, said: 'Spend, O son of Adam, and I will spend upon you.'" It is also established in the Sahih from his hadith, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "There is no day on which the servants rise except that two angels descend. One of them says, 'O God, give the one who spends a replacement,' and the other says, 'O God, give the one who withholds destruction.'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, say: "Indeed, every day has its misfortune, so repel the misfortune of that day with charity." Then he said: "Read the places of the replacement, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, say: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it,' so if you do not spend, how will it be replaced?"

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: "Indeed, aid descends from the sky in proportion to the expense."

Then He (glory be to Him) mentioned another kind of their disbelief, saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is, the Quranic verses, being clear in their indications and apparent in their meanings, they say: "This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship" — meaning the idols that your forefathers (aslaf) used to worship. Secondly, they said, referring to the Noble Qur'an: ﴿This is nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, that is, a invented falsehood. Thirdly, ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them﴾, that is, of the religion that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought: ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾. This denial from them concerns tawhid specifically; as for the denial of the Qur'an and the miracle, it was agreed upon among the People of the Book and the polytheists. It was said: the first, their saying ﴿nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, is intended to mean its meaning, and the second, their saying ﴿this is nothing but evident magic﴾, is intended to mean its miraculous composition (nazm).

It was said: some of them said it is a lie, and others said it is magic. It was also said: all of them at times said it is a lie and at other times said it is magic. The first view is preferable.

﴿And We did not give them any books which they study﴾, that is, We did not send down to the Arabs any heavenly books in which they study, ﴿nor did We send to them before you any warner﴾ who calls them to the truth and warns them of punishment. So there is no basis for their denial of the Qur'an and the Messenger, nor any doubt to which they can cling.

Qatadah said: Allah did not send down to the Arabs any book before the Qur'an, nor did He send to them any prophet before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Farra' said: that is, from where did they deny you, when no book or warner had come to them with this which they did?

Then He (glory be to Him) made them secure in their position and informed about their end and the end of those before them, saying: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach one-tenth of what We gave them﴾, that is, the people of Makkah, the polytheist Quraysh and others of the Arabs, did not reach a tenth of what We gave those before them of strength, abundance of wealth and long life; then Allah destroyed them, like 'Ad, Thamud and their likes.

Al-mi'shar is the tenth. Al-Jawhari said: the mi'shar of a thing is its tenth. It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of a tenth, and the first is preferable.

It was said: the meaning is: those before them did not reach a tenth of what We gave these people of clear proofs and guidance.

It was said: those before them did not reach a tenth of the thankfulness for what We gave them. It was also said: Allah did not give those before them a tenth of what He gave them of knowledge, eloquence, proof and evidence; and the first is preferable.

It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of the 'ashir, and the 'ashir is a tenth of a tenth, so it would be one part of a thousand parts.

Al-Mawardi said: and this is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is exaggeration in minimizing. I say: observing exaggeration in minimizing does not permit departing from the Arabic sense for its sake. His saying ﴿so they denied My messengers﴾ is a conjunction with "those before them denied", in the manner of explanation, like His saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar: 9], and so on. The better view is that it is a conjunction of the particular over the general, because the first denial, when its object is omitted, conveys generality. So its meaning is: they denied the revealed books, the sent messengers and the clear miracles; the denial of the messengers is more specific than that, although it entails it, but the verbal indication is observed, not the implied indication. ﴿So how was My denial﴾, that is, how was My punishment and retribution against them? Let these people beware of the like of that. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the estimate is: "So We destroyed them, so how was My denial", and nakir is a noun meaning denial (inkar).

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded His Messenger to establish against them a proof from which they cannot escape, saying: ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾, that is, I warn you and caution you of the evil end of what you are in, and I advise you with one matter, which is ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly﴾. This is an explanation of the one thing, or a substitute for it: it is your standing and your exertion in seeking the truth with sincere thought, scattered in twos and in ones, because gathering confuses thought. The intent is not standing on the feet, but standing in seeking the truth and sincerely reflecting on it, as one says: "So-and-so stood up to the matter", then reflect on the matter of the Prophet and what he brought of the Book, for then you will know that what is with your companion is not madness. That is because they used to say: "Muhammad is mad." So Allah (glory be to Him) said: Say to them, consider my command with one thing, which is that you stand before Allah, and in His essence gathered together, so that a man says to his companion, "Come, let us be sincere with one another: have we seen in this man any madness", that is, insanity, or have we tested him in lying? Then each one withdraws from his companion and reflects and considers, for in that there is what indicates that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful, and that he is a messenger from Allah, and that he is neither a liar, nor a magician, nor mad. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾, that is, he is only a warner to you before the Hour. It was said: the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement from Allah (glory be to Him), brought to draw attention to the manner of consideration and reflection: that so great a matter and so great a claim would not be undertaken by anyone except a madman who does not care what is said about him and what lie is attributed to him; yet they knew that he was the most intelligent of people, so it was necessary that they believe him in his claim, especially with the clear miracle joined to it and their consensus that he was not one who fabricates lies, nor had they tested him in a lie throughout his life and theirs.

It was said: it is possible that the "ma" in "ma bi-sahibikum" is interrogative, meaning: then reflect on what kind of sign of madness is in him. It was said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾ is "There is no god but Allah"; this is what Mujahid and al-Suddi said.

It was said: it is the Qur'an, because it gathers all admonitions; and the better view is what we mentioned first.

Al-Zajjaj said: the "an" in His saying "an taqumu" is in a position of nasb, meaning "li-an taqumu" (in order that you stand).

Al-Suddi said: the meaning of mathna wa-furada: alone with his opinion, and consulting others.

Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his kinsmen, and reflecting within himself.

It was said: mathna is the work of the day, and furada the work of the night; this was said by al-Mawardi. How dull this view is and how little benefit it has.

Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari preferred stopping at His saying ﴿then reflect﴾, and in that case the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement, as we have mentioned. It was said: it is not a pause, because the meaning is: "then reflect whether you tested him in a lie, or saw in him madness, or any corruption in his conduct."

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded that he inform them that he had no aim in this world nor desire for it, so that doubts would be cut off from them and suspicion removed, saying: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾, that is, whatever compensation I have asked of you in return for the message, it is yours if I have asked it of you. The intent is the negation of asking at all, as one says: "What I possess in this, I have given to you", meaning he has no ownership of it at all. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Say: I ask of you no reward for it except affection among kinsfolk﴾ [al-Shura: 23], and His saying: ﴿I ask of you no reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].

Then He explained to them that his reward is with Allah (glory be to Him), saying: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, that is, my reward is only from Allah, not from anyone else, ﴿and He is over all things a Witness﴾, that is, Watchful, nothing from anything escapes Him.

﴿Say: Indeed my Lord casts the truth; Knower of the unseen.﴾ Casting (ramy) is with an arrow, pebbles, and speech. Al-Kalbi said: "He casts" in the sense of "He brings it"; Muqatil said: He speaks the truth, which is the Qur'an and revelation, that is, He throws it to His prophets. Qatadah said: "with the truth," that is, with revelation; the meaning is that He makes the proof clear and manifests it to people through the tongues of His messengers. It was also said: He casts falsehood with truth so that it crushes it. ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾: the majority read "'Allam" with a raised vowel, as a second predicate of inna, or the predicate of an omitted subject, or a substitute for the pronoun in yaqdhifu, or in apposition to the place of inna's noun. Al-Zajjaj said: the raising is on two grounds, by place, since the place is a raised position, or by substitution.

Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with nasb as an adjective of the noun of inna, or as a substitute for it, or as an expression of praise. Al-Farra' said: raising in such a case is more common, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed that is true, the contention of the people of the Fire﴾ [Sad: 64]. "Al-ghuyub" is read with the three vowels on the ghayn; it is the plural of ghayb, and ghayb is that which has gone away and become very hidden.

﴿Say: the truth has come﴾, that is, Islam and tawhid. Qatadah said: the Qur'an.

Al-Nahhas said: the estimate is "the owner of the truth", that is, the Book in which are the proofs and arguments.

I say: there is no reason to estimate an omitted noun, for the Qur'an has come just as its owner has come. ﴿And falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾, that is, falsehood has gone away in such a way that nothing remains of it: no approach, nor retreat, nor origination, nor restoration. Qatadah said: falsehood is Satan, that is, Satan does not create anything from the beginning, nor does he resurrect; this is also what Muqatil and al-Kalbi said.

It was said: "ma" may be interrogative, meaning: what can he originate, and what can he restore? The first is preferable.

﴿Say: if I go astray﴾ from the true, clear path, ﴿then I only go astray against myself﴾, that is, the sin of my error falls upon myself. That is because the disbelievers said to him: "You left the religion of your fathers, so you have gone astray," and Allah commanded him to say this to them. ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ of wisdom, admonition, and clear explanation through the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed He is Hearing, Near﴾, near to me and to you, knowing guidance and error. The majority read "dalaltu" with a fatha on the lam; al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read it with a kasra on the lam, which is the dialect of the people of al-'Aliya.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and they did not reach a tenth of what We gave them﴾: he said, of strength in the world.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi regarding the verse: he said, a man stands with a man or alone, and reflects whether his companion has any madness.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾: he said, that he is not mad.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿whatever reward I have asked of you﴾: that is, of compensation, it is yours; he said: I did not ask you for a payment for Islam. Regarding ﴿Say: indeed my Lord casts the truth﴾: he said: by revelation. Regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Satan does not originate nor restore when he is destroyed.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Iblis does not create anything nor resurrect it.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Umar ibn Sa'd regarding ﴿if I go astray, I only go astray against myself﴾: he said, I am only held accountable for my own offense.

Then He (glory be to Him) mentioned another kind of their disbelief, saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is, the Quranic verses, being clear in their indications and apparent in their meanings, they say: "This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship" — meaning the idols that your forefathers (aslaf) used to worship. Secondly, they said, referring to the Noble Qur'an: ﴿This is nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, that is, a invented falsehood. Thirdly, ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them﴾, that is, of the religion that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought: ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾. This denial from them concerns tawhid specifically; as for the denial of the Qur'an and the miracle, it was agreed upon among the People of the Book and the polytheists. It was said: the first, their saying ﴿nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, is intended to mean its meaning, and the second, their saying ﴿this is nothing but evident magic﴾, is intended to mean its miraculous composition (nazm).

It was said: some of them said it is a lie, and others said it is magic. It was also said: all of them at times said it is a lie and at other times said it is magic. The first view is preferable.

﴿And We did not give them any books which they study﴾, that is, We did not send down to the Arabs any heavenly books in which they study, ﴿nor did We send to them before you any warner﴾ who calls them to the truth and warns them of punishment. So there is no basis for their denial of the Qur'an and the Messenger, nor any doubt to which they can cling.

Qatadah said: Allah did not send down to the Arabs any book before the Qur'an, nor did He send to them any prophet before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Farra' said: that is, from where did they deny you, when no book or warner had come to them with this which they did?

Then He (glory be to Him) made them secure in their position and informed about their end and the end of those before them, saying: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach one-tenth of what We gave them﴾, that is, the people of Makkah, the polytheist Quraysh and others of the Arabs, did not reach a tenth of what We gave those before them of strength, abundance of wealth and long life; then Allah destroyed them, like 'Ad, Thamud and their likes.

Al-mi'shar is the tenth. Al-Jawhari said: the mi'shar of a thing is its tenth. It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of a tenth, and the first is preferable.

It was said: the meaning is: those before them did not reach a tenth of what We gave these people of clear proofs and guidance.

It was said: those before them did not reach a tenth of the thankfulness for what We gave them. It was also said: Allah did not give those before them a tenth of what He gave them of knowledge, eloquence, proof and evidence; and the first is preferable.

It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of the 'ashir, and the 'ashir is a tenth of a tenth, so it would be one part of a thousand parts.

Al-Mawardi said: and this is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is exaggeration in minimizing. I say: observing exaggeration in minimizing does not permit departing from the Arabic sense for its sake. His saying ﴿so they denied My messengers﴾ is a conjunction with "those before them denied", in the manner of explanation, like His saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar: 9], and so on. The better view is that it is a conjunction of the particular over the general, because the first denial, when its object is omitted, conveys generality. So its meaning is: they denied the revealed books, the sent messengers and the clear miracles; the denial of the messengers is more specific than that, although it entails it, but the verbal indication is observed, not the implied indication. ﴿So how was My denial﴾, that is, how was My punishment and retribution against them? Let these people beware of the like of that. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the estimate is: "So We destroyed them, so how was My denial", and nakir is a noun meaning denial (inkar).

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded His Messenger to establish against them a proof from which they cannot escape, saying: ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾, that is, I warn you and caution you of the evil end of what you are in, and I advise you with one matter, which is ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly﴾. This is an explanation of the one thing, or a substitute for it: it is your standing and your exertion in seeking the truth with sincere thought, scattered in twos and in ones, because gathering confuses thought. The intent is not standing on the feet, but standing in seeking the truth and sincerely reflecting on it, as one says: "So-and-so stood up to the matter", then reflect on the matter of the Prophet and what he brought of the Book, for then you will know that what is with your companion is not madness. That is because they used to say: "Muhammad is mad." So Allah (glory be to Him) said: Say to them, consider my command with one thing, which is that you stand before Allah, and in His essence gathered together, so that a man says to his companion, "Come, let us be sincere with one another: have we seen in this man any madness", that is, insanity, or have we tested him in lying? Then each one withdraws from his companion and reflects and considers, for in that there is what indicates that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful, and that he is a messenger from Allah, and that he is neither a liar, nor a magician, nor mad. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾, that is, he is only a warner to you before the Hour. It was said: the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement from Allah (glory be to Him), brought to draw attention to the manner of consideration and reflection: that so great a matter and so great a claim would not be undertaken by anyone except a madman who does not care what is said about him and what lie is attributed to him; yet they knew that he was the most intelligent of people, so it was necessary that they believe him in his claim, especially with the clear miracle joined to it and their consensus that he was not one who fabricates lies, nor had they tested him in a lie throughout his life and theirs.

It was said: it is possible that the "ma" in "ma bi-sahibikum" is interrogative, meaning: then reflect on what kind of sign of madness is in him. It was said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾ is "There is no god but Allah"; this is what Mujahid and al-Suddi said.

It was said: it is the Qur'an, because it gathers all admonitions; and the better view is what we mentioned first.

Al-Zajjaj said: the "an" in His saying "an taqumu" is in a position of nasb, meaning "li-an taqumu" (in order that you stand).

Al-Suddi said: the meaning of mathna wa-furada: alone with his opinion, and consulting others.

Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his kinsmen, and reflecting within himself.

It was said: mathna is the work of the day, and furada the work of the night; this was said by al-Mawardi. How dull this view is and how little benefit it has.

Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari preferred stopping at His saying ﴿then reflect﴾, and in that case the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement, as we have mentioned. It was said: it is not a pause, because the meaning is: "then reflect whether you tested him in a lie, or saw in him madness, or any corruption in his conduct."

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded that he inform them that he had no aim in this world nor desire for it, so that doubts would be cut off from them and suspicion removed, saying: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾, that is, whatever compensation I have asked of you in return for the message, it is yours if I have asked it of you. The intent is the negation of asking at all, as one says: "What I possess in this, I have given to you", meaning he has no ownership of it at all. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Say: I ask of you no reward for it except affection among kinsfolk﴾ [al-Shura: 23], and His saying: ﴿I ask of you no reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].

Then He explained to them that his reward is with Allah (glory be to Him), saying: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, that is, my reward is only from Allah, not from anyone else, ﴿and He is over all things a Witness﴾, that is, Watchful, nothing from anything escapes Him.

Al-Farra' said: that is, from where did they deny you, when no book or warner had come to them with this which they did?

Al-Mawardi said: and this is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is exaggeration in minimizing. I say: observing exaggeration in minimizing does not permit departing from the Arabic sense for its sake. His saying ﴿so they denied My messengers﴾ is a conjunction with "those before them denied", in the manner of explanation, like His saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar: 9], and so on. The better view is that it is a conjunction of the particular over the general, because the first denial, when its object is omitted, conveys generality. So its meaning is: they denied the revealed books, the sent messengers and the clear miracles; the denial of the messengers is more specific than that, although it entails it, but the verbal indication is observed, not the implied indication. ﴿So how was My denial﴾, that is, how was My punishment and retribution against them? Let these people beware of the like of that. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the estimate is: "So We destroyed them, so how was My denial", and nakir is a noun meaning denial (inkar).

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded His Messenger to establish against them a proof from which they cannot escape, saying: ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾, that is, I warn you and caution you of the evil end of what you are in, and I advise you with one matter, which is ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly﴾. This is an explanation of the one thing, or a substitute for it: it is your standing and your exertion in seeking the truth with sincere thought, scattered in twos and in ones, because gathering confuses thought. The intent is not standing on the feet, but standing in seeking the truth and sincerely reflecting on it, as one says: "So-and-so stood up to the matter", then reflect on the matter of the Prophet and what he brought of the Book, for then you will know that what is with your companion is not madness. That is because they used to say: "Muhammad is mad." So Allah (glory be to Him) said: Say to them, consider my command with one thing, which is that you stand before Allah, and in His essence gathered together, so that a man says to his companion, "Come, let us be sincere with one another: have we seen in this man any madness", that is, insanity, or have we tested him in lying? Then each one withdraws from his companion and reflects and considers, for in that there is what indicates that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful, and that he is a messenger from Allah, and that he is neither a liar, nor a magician, nor mad. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾, that is, he is only a warner to you before the Hour. It was said: the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement from Allah (glory be to Him), brought to draw attention to the manner of consideration and reflection: that so great a matter and so great a claim would not be undertaken by anyone except a madman who does not care what is said about him and what lie is attributed to him; yet they knew that he was the most intelligent of people, so it was necessary that they believe him in his claim, especially with the clear miracle joined to it and their consensus that he was not one who fabricates lies, nor had they tested him in a lie throughout his life and theirs.

It was said: it is possible that the "ma" in "ma bi-sahibikum" is interrogative, meaning: then reflect on what kind of sign of madness is in him. It was said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾ is "There is no god but Allah"; this is what Mujahid and al-Suddi said.

It was said: it is the Qur'an, because it gathers all admonitions; and the better view is what we mentioned first.

Al-Zajjaj said: the "an" in His saying "an taqumu" is in a position of nasb, meaning "li-an taqumu" (in order that you stand).

Al-Suddi said: the meaning of mathna wa-furada: alone with his opinion, and consulting others.

Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his kinsmen, and reflecting within himself.

It was said: mathna is the work of the day, and furada the work of the night; this was said by al-Mawardi. How dull this view is and how little benefit it has.

Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari preferred stopping at His saying ﴿then reflect﴾, and in that case the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement, as we have mentioned. It was said: it is not a pause, because the meaning is: "then reflect whether you tested him in a lie, or saw in him madness, or any corruption in his conduct."

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded that he inform them that he had no aim in this world nor desire for it, so that doubts would be cut off from them and suspicion removed, saying: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾, that is, whatever compensation I have asked of you in return for the message, it is yours if I have asked it of you. The intent is the negation of asking at all, as one says: "What I possess in this, I have given to you", meaning he has no ownership of it at all. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Say: I ask of you no reward for it except affection among kinsfolk﴾ [al-Shura: 23], and His saying: ﴿I ask of you no reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].

Then He explained to them that his reward is with Allah (glory be to Him), saying: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, that is, my reward is only from Allah, not from anyone else, ﴿and He is over all things a Witness﴾, that is, Watchful, nothing from anything escapes Him.

﴿Say: Indeed my Lord casts the truth; Knower of the unseen.﴾ Casting (ramy) is with an arrow, pebbles, and speech. Al-Kalbi said: "He casts" in the sense of "He brings it"; Muqatil said: He speaks the truth, which is the Qur'an and revelation, that is, He throws it to His prophets. Qatadah said: "with the truth," that is, with revelation; the meaning is that He makes the proof clear and manifests it to people through the tongues of His messengers. It was also said: He casts falsehood with truth so that it crushes it. ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾: the majority read "'Allam" with a raised vowel, as a second predicate of inna, or the predicate of an omitted subject, or a substitute for the pronoun in yaqdhifu, or in apposition to the place of inna's noun. Al-Zajjaj said: the raising is on two grounds, by place, since the place is a raised position, or by substitution.

Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with nasb as an adjective of the noun of inna, or as a substitute for it, or as an expression of praise. Al-Farra' said: raising in such a case is more common, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed that is true, the contention of the people of the Fire﴾ [Sad: 64]. "Al-ghuyub" is read with the three vowels on the ghayn; it is the plural of ghayb, and ghayb is that which has gone away and become very hidden.

﴿Say: the truth has come﴾, that is, Islam and tawhid. Qatadah said: the Qur'an.

Al-Nahhas said: the estimate is "the owner of the truth", that is, the Book in which are the proofs and arguments.

I say: there is no reason to estimate an omitted noun, for the Qur'an has come just as its owner has come. ﴿And falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾, that is, falsehood has gone away in such a way that nothing remains of it: no approach, nor retreat, nor origination, nor restoration. Qatadah said: falsehood is Satan, that is, Satan does not create anything from the beginning, nor does he resurrect; this is also what Muqatil and al-Kalbi said.

It was said: "ma" may be interrogative, meaning: what can he originate, and what can he restore? The first is preferable.

﴿Say: if I go astray﴾ from the true, clear path, ﴿then I only go astray against myself﴾, that is, the sin of my error falls upon myself. That is because the disbelievers said to him: "You left the religion of your fathers, so you have gone astray," and Allah commanded him to say this to them. ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ of wisdom, admonition, and clear explanation through the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed He is Hearing, Near﴾, near to me and to you, knowing guidance and error. The majority read "dalaltu" with a fatha on the lam; al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read it with a kasra on the lam, which is the dialect of the people of al-'Aliya.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and they did not reach a tenth of what We gave them﴾: he said, of strength in the world.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi regarding the verse: he said, a man stands with a man or alone, and reflects whether his companion has any madness.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾: he said, that he is not mad.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿whatever reward I have asked of you﴾: that is, of compensation, it is yours; he said: I did not ask you for a payment for Islam. Regarding ﴿Say: indeed my Lord casts the truth﴾: he said: by revelation. Regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Satan does not originate nor restore when he is destroyed.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Iblis does not create anything nor resurrect it.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Umar ibn Sa'd regarding ﴿if I go astray, I only go astray against myself﴾: he said, I am only held accountable for my own offense.

Then He (glory be to Him) mentioned another kind of their disbelief, saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is, the Quranic verses, being clear in their indications and apparent in their meanings, they say: "This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship" — meaning the idols that your forefathers (aslaf) used to worship. Secondly, they said, referring to the Noble Qur'an: ﴿This is nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, that is, a invented falsehood. Thirdly, ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them﴾, that is, of the religion that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought: ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾. This denial from them concerns tawhid specifically; as for the denial of the Qur'an and the miracle, it was agreed upon among the People of the Book and the polytheists. It was said: the first, their saying ﴿nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, is intended to mean its meaning, and the second, their saying ﴿this is nothing but evident magic﴾, is intended to mean its miraculous composition (nazm).

It was said: some of them said it is a lie, and others said it is magic. It was also said: all of them at times said it is a lie and at other times said it is magic. The first view is preferable.

﴿And We did not give them any books which they study﴾, that is, We did not send down to the Arabs any heavenly books in which they study, ﴿nor did We send to them before you any warner﴾ who calls them to the truth and warns them of punishment. So there is no basis for their denial of the Qur'an and the Messenger, nor any doubt to which they can cling.

Qatadah said: Allah did not send down to the Arabs any book before the Qur'an, nor did He send to them any prophet before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Farra' said: that is, from where did they deny you, when no book or warner had come to them with this which they did?

Then He (glory be to Him) made them secure in their position and informed about their end and the end of those before them, saying: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach one-tenth of what We gave them﴾, that is, the people of Makkah, the polytheist Quraysh and others of the Arabs, did not reach a tenth of what We gave those before them of strength, abundance of wealth and long life; then Allah destroyed them, like 'Ad, Thamud and their likes.

Al-mi'shar is the tenth. Al-Jawhari said: the mi'shar of a thing is its tenth. It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of a tenth, and the first is preferable.

It was said: the meaning is: those before them did not reach a tenth of what We gave these people of clear proofs and guidance.

It was said: those before them did not reach a tenth of the thankfulness for what We gave them. It was also said: Allah did not give those before them a tenth of what He gave them of knowledge, eloquence, proof and evidence; and the first is preferable.

It was said: al-mi'shar is a tenth of the 'ashir, and the 'ashir is a tenth of a tenth, so it would be one part of a thousand parts.

Al-Mawardi said: and this is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is exaggeration in minimizing. I say: observing exaggeration in minimizing does not permit departing from the Arabic sense for its sake. His saying ﴿so they denied My messengers﴾ is a conjunction with "those before them denied", in the manner of explanation, like His saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant﴾ [al-Qamar: 9], and so on. The better view is that it is a conjunction of the particular over the general, because the first denial, when its object is omitted, conveys generality. So its meaning is: they denied the revealed books, the sent messengers and the clear miracles; the denial of the messengers is more specific than that, although it entails it, but the verbal indication is observed, not the implied indication. ﴿So how was My denial﴾, that is, how was My punishment and retribution against them? Let these people beware of the like of that. It was said: there is an omission in the speech, and the estimate is: "So We destroyed them, so how was My denial", and nakir is a noun meaning denial (inkar).

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded His Messenger to establish against them a proof from which they cannot escape, saying: ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾, that is, I warn you and caution you of the evil end of what you are in, and I advise you with one matter, which is ﴿that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly﴾. This is an explanation of the one thing, or a substitute for it: it is your standing and your exertion in seeking the truth with sincere thought, scattered in twos and in ones, because gathering confuses thought. The intent is not standing on the feet, but standing in seeking the truth and sincerely reflecting on it, as one says: "So-and-so stood up to the matter", then reflect on the matter of the Prophet and what he brought of the Book, for then you will know that what is with your companion is not madness. That is because they used to say: "Muhammad is mad." So Allah (glory be to Him) said: Say to them, consider my command with one thing, which is that you stand before Allah, and in His essence gathered together, so that a man says to his companion, "Come, let us be sincere with one another: have we seen in this man any madness", that is, insanity, or have we tested him in lying? Then each one withdraws from his companion and reflects and considers, for in that there is what indicates that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful, and that he is a messenger from Allah, and that he is neither a liar, nor a magician, nor mad. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾, that is, he is only a warner to you before the Hour. It was said: the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement from Allah (glory be to Him), brought to draw attention to the manner of consideration and reflection: that so great a matter and so great a claim would not be undertaken by anyone except a madman who does not care what is said about him and what lie is attributed to him; yet they knew that he was the most intelligent of people, so it was necessary that they believe him in his claim, especially with the clear miracle joined to it and their consensus that he was not one who fabricates lies, nor had they tested him in a lie throughout his life and theirs.

It was said: it is possible that the "ma" in "ma bi-sahibikum" is interrogative, meaning: then reflect on what kind of sign of madness is in him. It was said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Say: I only admonish you with one thing﴾ is "There is no god but Allah"; this is what Mujahid and al-Suddi said.

It was said: it is the Qur'an, because it gathers all admonitions; and the better view is what we mentioned first.

Al-Zajjaj said: the "an" in His saying "an taqumu" is in a position of nasb, meaning "li-an taqumu" (in order that you stand).

Al-Suddi said: the meaning of mathna wa-furada: alone with his opinion, and consulting others.

Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his kinsmen, and reflecting within himself.

It was said: mathna is the work of the day, and furada the work of the night; this was said by al-Mawardi. How dull this view is and how little benefit it has.

Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari preferred stopping at His saying ﴿then reflect﴾, and in that case the clause ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾ is a fresh statement, as we have mentioned. It was said: it is not a pause, because the meaning is: "then reflect whether you tested him in a lie, or saw in him madness, or any corruption in his conduct."

Then Allah (glory be to Him) commanded that he inform them that he had no aim in this world nor desire for it, so that doubts would be cut off from them and suspicion removed, saying: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾, that is, whatever compensation I have asked of you in return for the message, it is yours if I have asked it of you. Then He explained to them that his reward is with Allah (glory be to Him), saying: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, that is, my reward is only from Allah, not from anyone else, ﴿and He is over all things a Witness﴾, that is, Watchful, nothing from anything escapes Him.

Al-Kalbi said: "He casts" in the sense of "He brings it"; Muqatil said: He speaks the truth, which is the Qur'an and revelation, that is, He throws it to His prophets. Qatadah said: "with the truth," that is, with revelation; the meaning is that He makes the proof clear and manifests it to people through the tongues of His messengers. Al-Zajjaj said: the raising is on two grounds, by place, since the place is a raised position, or by substitution.

Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with nasb as an adjective of the noun of inna, or as a substitute for it, or as an expression of praise. Al-Farra' said: raising in such a case is more common, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed that is true, the contention of the people of the Fire﴾ [Sad: 64]. "Al-ghuyub" is read with the three vowels on the ghayn; it is the plural of ghayb, and ghayb is that which has gone away and become very hidden.

﴿Say: the truth has come﴾, that is, Islam and tawhid. Qatadah said: the Qur'an.

Al-Nahhas said: the estimate is "the owner of the truth", that is, the Book in which are the proofs and arguments.

I say: there is no reason to estimate an omitted noun, for the Qur'an has come just as its owner has come. ﴿And falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾, that is, falsehood has gone away in such a way that nothing remains of it: no approach, nor retreat, nor origination, nor restoration. Qatadah said: falsehood is Satan, that is, Satan does not create anything from the beginning, nor does he resurrect; this is also what Muqatil and al-Kalbi said.

It was said: "ma" may be interrogative, meaning: what can he originate, and what can he restore? The first is preferable.

﴿Say: if I go astray﴾ from the true, clear path, ﴿then I only go astray against myself﴾, that is, the sin of my error falls upon myself. That is because the disbelievers said to him: "You left the religion of your fathers, so you have gone astray," and Allah commanded him to say this to them. ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ of wisdom, admonition, and clear explanation through the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed He is Hearing, Near﴾, near to me and to you, knowing guidance and error. The majority read "dalaltu" with a fatha on the lam; al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Wathhab read it with a kasra on the lam, which is the dialect of the people of al-'Aliya.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and they did not reach a tenth of what We gave them﴾: he said, of strength in the world.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi regarding the verse: he said, a man stands with a man or alone, and reflects whether his companion has any madness.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding ﴿what is with your companion of madness﴾: he said, that he is not mad.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿whatever reward I have asked of you﴾: that is, of compensation, it is yours; he said: I did not ask you for a payment for Islam. Regarding ﴿Say: indeed my Lord casts the truth﴾: he said: by revelation. Regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Satan does not originate nor restore when he is destroyed.

These also transmitted from him regarding ﴿falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾: he said: Iblis does not create anything nor resurrect it.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from 'Umar ibn Sa'd regarding ﴿if I go astray, I only go astray against myself﴾: he said, I am only held accountable for my own offense.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned a state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified﴾. The address is to the Messenger of Allah, or to everyone who is fit for it. It has been said: what is meant is their terror at the coming of death upon them.

Al-Hasan said: it is their terror in the graves at the Blast (al-sayhah). Qatadah said: it is their terror when they come out of their graves.

Al-Suddi said: it is their terror on the Day of Badr, when their necks were struck by the swords of the angels, so they could not escape nor return to repentance.

Ibn Mughaffal said: it is their terror when they witness the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the sinking into the earth (al-khasf) that will befall them in the desert (al-bayda'), so one man of them will remain and inform the people of what befell his companions, and they will be terrified.

The answer to "law" (if) is omitted, meaning: you would see a terrifying matter. The meaning of ﴿then there is no escape﴾ is: none of them will escape Me, and none of them will be saved.

Mujahid said: ﴿then there is no escape﴾ means there is no place of flight, and they will be seized from a near place, either from the surface of the earth, or from the graves, or from the place of reckoning. It was also said: from where they were, so they are near to Allah and cannot get far from Him or escape Him.

It has been said: it is possible that this terror is the terror that carries the meaning of answering, as one says: "fazi'a al-rajul" when he answers the one crying for help who seeks their aid, like their rushing to war on the Day of Badr.

They said: "We believe in Him," that is, in Muhammad, as Qatadah said, or in the Qur'an.

Mujahid said: "in Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Al-Hasan said: "in the Resurrection." ﴿And how can they reach [the faith] from a distant place?﴾ Al-tanawush (reaching) means taking hold, and it is a form of tafa'ul from al-tanawush, which is taking. The meaning is: how can they take hold of faith after [this], that is, in the Hereafter, when they had abandoned it in the world? This is the meaning of "from a distant place," and it is a parable of their state in seeking deliverance after what has passed them by.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: it is said of a man who reaches for another man to take hold of his head or his beard: "nasha yanushuhu nawshan." He recited:

"So she reaches for the water of the pool from above, a reaching by which she cuts across the wide deserts."

That is: she reaches for the water of the pool from above. From this comes "munawasha" (skirmishing) in fighting. It was also said: al-tanawush means return, that is: how can they return to the world so that they may believe? From this is the saying of the poet:

"May Mayy wish to return to me, but there is no way to reach her."

The clause ﴿and they had already disbelieved in it before﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while they had already disbelieved in what they now believe in, before this time, and that was while they were in the world.

Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and al-A'mash read "al-tana'ush" with a hamza, while the rest read it with a waw. Abu 'Ubayd and al-Nahhas considered the first reading unlikely, but there is no basis for that unlikelihood, for it is established in the language and poetry of the Arabs. From this is the saying of the poet:

"You sat for a time away from your pursuit of high station, and you came late (na'ish) after the good had passed you by."

That is: "and you came late (akhira)."

Al-Farra' said: hamzing and not hamzing are close in meaning. ﴿And they cast [at] the unseen﴾, that is: they hurl at random with conjecture, saying: there is no resurrection, no rising, no Paradise, and no Fire, ﴿from a distant place﴾, that is: from a far-off place in which there is no basis for their false conjecture.

It was also said: the meaning is: they say false things about the Qur'an: that it is sorcery, poetry, and the fables of the ancients.

It was also said: they say about Muhammad: he is a sorcerer, a poet, a soothsayer, a madman.

Abu Haywah, Mujahid, and Mahbub from Abu 'Amr read "yuqdhafun" in the passive voice, meaning: they are pelted with what grieves them as a result of their deeds, from where they do not expect. In this there is a parable of their state with the state of one who throws something he does not see from a far place, where there is no room for the illusion of its reaching. The clause is either coordinated with "and they had already disbelieved in it," as a narration of a past state and a bringing of its image to mind, or it is a new clause explaining the parable of their state.

﴿And there will be a barrier between them and what they desire﴾ of salvation from the punishment; they are prevented from that. It was also said: a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire in the world of their wealth and their families, or a barrier between them and what they desire of returning to the world. ﴿As was done with their like before﴾, that is: with their counterparts and peers among the disbelievers of earlier nations. "Ashya'" is the plural of "shiya'," and "shiya'" is the plural of "shi'ah." The clause ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾ is a reason for what precedes it, that is: in a doubt that produces suspicion, or one that has suspicion, concerning the matter of the Messengers, the Resurrection, Paradise, and the Fire, or concerning monotheism and the religion the Messengers brought. It is said: "arāba al-rajul" when a man becomes one with suspicion, so he is "murib." It was also said: it is from "al-rayb," which is doubt, so it is like one says "a wondrous wonder" and "a poem that is poetic."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿then there is no escape﴾ that he said: "then there is no deliverance."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding His words ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, then there is no escape and they are seized from a near place﴾ that he said: "It is the army of al-Sufyani." It was asked: "From where are they seized?" He said: "From beneath their feet."

It is established in the Sahih that an army will be swallowed up in the desert, from the hadith of Hafsah and 'A'ishah, and outside the Sahih from the hadith of Umm Salamah, Safiyyah, Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Mas'ud. None of them states that this is the occasion of revelation of this verse. However, Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman the story of this sinking, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and at its end he said: "That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, in Surah Saba': ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, then there is no escape﴾," and the verse.

Al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿And how can they reach [the faith] from a distant place?﴾ that he said: "How can they have the return from a distant place?" He said: "They ask for return, but it is not a time for return."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Taymi, who said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "What is al-tanawush?" He said: "The reaching for a thing, and it is not the time for that."

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned a state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified﴾. The address is to the Messenger of Allah, or to everyone who is fit for it. It has been said: what is meant is their terror at the coming of death upon them.

Al-Hasan said: it is their terror in the graves at the Blast (al-sayhah). Qatadah said: it is their terror when they come out of their graves.

Al-Suddi said: it is their terror on the Day of Badr, when their necks were struck by the swords of the angels, so they could not escape nor return to repentance.

Ibn Mughaffal said: it is their terror when they witness the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the sinking into the earth (al-khasf) that will befall them in the desert (al-bayda'), so one man of them will remain and inform the people of what befell his companions, and they will be terrified.

The answer to "law" (if) is omitted, meaning: you would see a terrifying matter. The meaning of ﴿then there is no escape﴾ is: none of them will escape Me, and none of them will be saved.

Mujahid said: ﴿then there is no escape﴾ means there is no place of flight, and they will be seized from a near place, either from the surface of the earth, or from the graves, or from the place of reckoning. It was also said: from where they were, so they are near to Allah and cannot get far from Him or escape Him.

It has been said: it is possible that this terror is the terror that carries the meaning of answering, as one says: "fazi'a al-rajul" when he answers the one crying for help who seeks their aid, like their rushing to war on the Day of Badr.

They said: "We believe in Him," that is, in Muhammad, as Qatadah said, or in the Qur'an.

Mujahid said: "in Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Al-Hasan said: "in the Resurrection." ﴿And how can they reach [the faith] from a distant place?﴾ Al-tanawush (reaching) means taking hold, and it is a form of tafa'ul from al-tanawush, which is taking. The meaning is: how can they take hold of faith after [this], that is, in the Hereafter, when they had abandoned it in the world? This is the meaning of "from a distant place," and it is a parable of their state in seeking deliverance after what has passed them by.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: it is said of a man who reaches for another man to take hold of his head or his beard: "nasha yanushuhu nawshan." He recited:

"So she reaches for the water of the pool from above, a reaching by which she cuts across the wide deserts."

That is: she reaches for the water of the pool from above. From this comes "munawasha" (skirmishing) in fighting. It was also said: al-tanawush means return, that is: how can they return to the world so that they may believe? From this is the saying of the poet:

"May Mayy wish to return to me, but there is no way to reach her."

Abu 'Ubayd and al-Nahhas considered the first reading unlikely, but there is no basis for that unlikelihood, for it is established in the language and poetry of the Arabs. From this is the saying of the poet:

That is: "and you came late (akhira)."

It was also said: the meaning is: they say false things about the Qur'an: that it is sorcery, poetry, and the fables of the ancients.

It was also said: they say about Muhammad: he is a sorcerer, a poet, a soothsayer, a madman.
